title: President Trump on expensive NBA Finals tickets: ‘That’s the way life goes’
content:
President Donald Trump is scheduled to attend Game 3 of the NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden on Monday, but he didn’t have much to say about regular fans needing thousands of dollars to enter the building, too.

StubHub’s cheapest ticket for a single seat to the game between the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs was $9,771 as of Friday afternoon. Asked about the high prices by a reporter on Friday, Trump suggested folks who cannot afford to attend should watch at home.

“They can watch it on television. It’s sort of semi-free to watch it on television, but that’s the way life goes,” Trump said while speaking to reporters aboard Air Force One. He also praised the Knicks’ undefeated playoff streak thus far, singling out Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns as “fantastic.”

Game 3 will air live on ABC, so anyone with access to local TV should be able to watch with few obstacles. Streaming services such as YouTube TV and Hulu will also run Monday night’s game.

Trump previously said New York Knicks governor James Dolan invited him to attend a playoff game, commenting that he was interested in seeing the Knicks play in the finals. Now, for the first time in 27 years, the Knicks will host a finals game.

The last sitting president to attend an NBA game was President Barack Obama in 2015, when he saw his Chicago Bulls host the Cleveland Cavaliers. Trump will be the first president to attend an NBA Finals game.

Trump attended the Super Bowl between the Kansas City Chiefs and Philadelphia Eagles in 2025. In January, he attended the College Football Playoff championship game between Indiana and Miami in Miami Gardens, Fla.

Both the Knicks and Spurs are wearing “America250” patches on their jerseys during the NBA Finals to commemorate the nation’s 250th birthday. The anniversary of the nation’s founding also coincides with the FIFA World Cup, which starts June 11 and will include games in the U.S., Canada and Mexico.

FIFA has also faced criticism for the high prices of World Cup tickets ahead of the tournament’s start. Face-value tickets for this summer’s World Cup final at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, N.J., cost around $10,000.
